Q: What language do I choose? A:

If you already know Java and want something more modern in VS Code:

Go

  • Fast to learn & build with

  • Clean syntax

  • Great for backend, APIs, and tools

  • Productivity-focused

Rust

  • Super fast & memory-safe

  • Modern features (traits, enums, pattern matching)

  • Steeper learning curve

  • Great for systems/performance-heavy apps

Kotlin

  • Basically Java, but way nicer

  • Full OOP

  • Great for Android & JVM backend

My take:

Go = productivity
Rust = depth & performance
Kotlin = better Java

Q: Find all `*.html` but not `*.tpl.html` using JavaScript regex A: 
^.*\.html(?<!\.tpl\.html)$

For fun, a solution without lookarounds:

^
(?: .{1,3}
|   .* (?: [^.]...
       |   \.
           (?: [^t]..
           |   t
               (?: [^p].
               |   p
                   [^l]
               )
           )
       )
)
\.html
$

Q: Download satellite/maps images (from Google Maps or Live Maps?) A:

enter image description here

It's interesting to see how long people have been looking for ways to download map and location photos. Back in the day, many solutions relied on directly fetching map tiles, but nowadays most users are actually looking for an easier way to save photos from Google Maps business listings rather than downloading the map itself.

For anyone who finds this thread years later, there are now browser-based tools that simplify the process without requiring developers to calculate tile coordinates or work with map servers. I've been using DownloadMapImage.com to save photos from Google Maps listings and locations, which is much easier than the older tile-downloading approaches discussed here.

The landscape has changed a lot since 2009, but the need to extract location photos is still very much alive. 😄

Q: Checking whether a number is positive or negative using bitwise operators A:

if you wanna doing something exotic without caring about where the signbit is then you can use exponentiation :

let b = !n

return (-!b) ** (n < b)

No hard coded reference values to compare against either. The input itself is never directly negated (to avoid the wraparound issues with certain data types). The exponentiation base is the value normalized to either (-1) for anything non-zero, or (0) for zero itself. The exponent is a boolean expression that actually is comparing different things depending on the input. When input is non-zero, the expression normalizes to (n < 0), i.e. whether n is negative, but when input is +/- 0, then it becomes (0 < 1), which is always true.

That leads to these 3 outcome scenarios :

negatives := (-1) ** (n < 0) = (-1) ** (1) = -1
any zero  := (+0) ** (0 < 1) = (+0) ** (1) =  0
positives := (-1) ** (n < 0) = (-1) ** (0) = +1

These even work for +/-inf, but always return +1 for NaNs of any sign.

Q: Squarespace live server installation command failed (Windows 11) A:

I went deep down a rabbit hole, used npm install -g @squarespace/server --ignore scripts during the install since it was rejecting the Java download, refusing to use my Java declaration, and decided to try and bundle myself.

Then I got here:

C:\Users\MEEEEE\AppData\Roaming\npm\node_modules\@squarespace\server>npm run build
> @squarespace/server@1.10.3 build
> node scripts/assertall.js --notos=win32 && scripts/build.sh && npm run patch
Assertion failed: notos=win32

The thing is set to fail on Windows.

I used WSL to run Ubuntu 24, got node, got npm, ran a fresh npm install -g @squarespace/server but there were Windows path leak issues during that install attempt. Fixed via:

Step 1 — temporarily clean PATH (current session)

Run this inside WSL:

export PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin

Step 2 — confirm isolation

Now run:

which node
which npm

Expected:

/usr/bin/node
/usr/bin/npm

If not, Node is still partially Windows-linked and must be reinstalled.

Step 3 — move OUT of Windows filesystem (critical)

Do NOT install from /mnt/c/...

Run:

mkdir -p ~/projects
cp -r ~/sqstest ~/projects/
cd ~/projects/sqstest

Step 4 — verify clean environment

Run:

echo $PATH

It should NO LONGER contain:

  • /mnt/c/Program Files/...

  • /mnt/c/WINDOWS/...

  • /mnt/c/Users/...

Step 5 — reinstall clean

rm -rf node_modules package-lock.json
npm install @squarespace/server

And viola. No issues. No Windows leak. The package is clearly meant to reject Windows OS -- which is crazy because I have it running on another Windows machine when I installed it in 2025.

Going to spend the next few days trying to convince the client to get off Squarespace.

Q: Learning with Ai with out becoming dependent on it or lazy A:

Accepting that AI has made us lazy not to do anything is the FIRST step in progress. Hence start small and celebrate yr progress daily to keep motivated.

Start with simple CRUD and use AI to do auto-complete... The CRUD should target some of yr own need like budget/tasklist to get involved and feel the effort is useful beyond learning. Also use AI to generate yr own backlog of the features u want in yr app by conversing with some chatbots to generate the descriptions and acceptance criteria.
